title: Maximum photoelectron energy against frequency
caption: Einstein's equation KE_max = hf − φ is a straight line of gradient h (0.414 eV per 10¹⁴ Hz = h/e per volt of stopping potential), the same for every metal; only the threshold f₀ = φ/h moves. Zinc (φ = 4.3 eV) needs f > 10.4 × 10¹⁴ Hz. For 250 nm light (f = 12.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz, 4.96 eV) its electrons leave with at most 0.66 eV.
alt: Graph of maximum kinetic energy in electronvolts against frequency in units of 10^14 hertz: three parallel straight lines for caesium, sodium and zinc crossing zero at 5.1, 5.6 and 10.4 and rising with the same gradient; the 250 nm point on the zinc line is at 0.66 electronvolts.
description: The horizontal axis is the frequency of the light in units of 10¹⁴ Hz; the vertical axis is the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons in eV.
Each line is KE_max = hf − φ with gradient h = 0.414 eV per 10¹⁴ Hz, so the lines are parallel.
They meet the axis at the threshold frequencies: caesium (2.1 eV) 5.1, sodium (2.3 eV) 5.6 and zinc (4.3 eV) 10.4 × 10¹⁴ Hz. Below threshold no electrons are emitted whatever the intensity.
250 nm light has f = 12.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz, so on the zinc line KE_max = 0.66 eV.
